title: Health stability and behavior: utilization of population-based cancer screenings among South Asian immigrants in Germany
summary: People with migration background in Germany do not attend population-based cancer screenings as often as local residents. Determining the factors of non-utilization of these offers can help understand the barriers and facilitators for the successful integration of new service users into cancer-related healthcare services.  This mixed-methods study aims to understand the health behavior of South Asian migrants that influences their uptake of cancer screenings in Germany. The primary goal is to determine the utilization rates of population-based cancer screenings among South Asian immigrants, their sociodemographic characteristics and their health beliefs and behaviors. Quantitative and qualitative results are compared and integrated together for in-depth analysis. We aim to determine age- and gender-specific physical, psychological and sociocultural factors that influence behavior of South Asian immigrants towards cancer prevention services in Germany.
conditions: Health Belief Model; health behaviors; healthcare access; cancer screenings

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:

Exclusion criteria:
Lack of legal age of consent. Ineligibility (by age) to utilize population-based cancer screenings. Other nationalities than South Asian.
